pos.personaBrief: Stoke were willing to cede possession and 'pack it in defensively' (ESPN), and Cullis applied the 'percentage principle' of hitting the box faster and more often (Wolves history): danger matters, not the ball.

pro.personaBrief: The ball goes 'hoch und weit' past midfield to a strong centre-forward (Spielverlagerung, de.wikipedia); Cullis stressed long passes and speed of execution, and Pulis's full-backs played it diagonal after more than one touch (Higginbotham).

est.personaBrief: Pulis did 'a lot of shape' and 'everybody knew what was expected' and where the ball was going (Higginbotham); the target man is a fixed focal point (APFA) and Wolves' wingers stayed wide for long balls into space (Game of the People).

lar.personaBrief: Cullis's long balls went into space for onrushing wingers Hancocks and Mullen, and Stoke's diagonals and Delap throws fed aerial targets in the box: the route is wide and in the air, not through central combination.

blo.personaBrief: Teams won the ball in their own half before going long (Spielverlagerung); Stoke packed it in with tight defences and Pulis was 'a master of the 1-0 win' (ESPN, These Football Times), while goals came from set pieces rather than high regains (APFA: 45-50% from dead balls).

mar.personaBrief: No source states the marking scheme; inferred from a compact, deep British block built on simple, clear responsibilities ('simplicity is genius') and aerial duels in the box.

pla.personaBrief: Stoke kept the same repetitive plan every game and scored late by wearing opponents down (Higginbotham); Cullis even watered the pitch to force his own direct game on Honved, though Allardyce says he tweaks the team to suit opponents.

res.personaBrief: Pulis's Stoke were 'a byword for boring' yet masters of the 1-0, and Delap's throws were valued for points that 'kept us up' (ESPN): results first, aesthetics irrelevant.

sis.personaBrief: A drilled, repetitive plan where 'everybody knew what was expected' (Higginbotham) and Allardyce's data and POMO system turned free transfers and veterans into a 6th-placed side; talent like Djorkaeff was a 'bit of magic' on top of the system.

jog.personaBrief: Cullis placed 'huge emphasis on fitness and power' relying on 'fitness, pace and aggression', and Stoke were a very large, physical side strong in the air (Game of the People, ESPN).

bas.personaBrief: Allardyce built Bolton on veterans such as Hierro (36), Speed (35), Hendry (35), Okocha and Campo (Wikipedia, APFA): experience bought cheaply over academy development.

lid.personaBrief: Clear managerial authority with delegated staff and stat-based targets reviewed every 10 games (Training Ground Guru), and a demanding, hard-work culture from Buckley and Cullis (Wolves history).
